patches.rationale: The current implementation uses zero-based slicing (start = page * page_size), so page 2 size 2 on range(1,8) returns [5,6] instead of [3,4]. Fix by making the slice one-based: start = (page - 1) * page_size. The guard for page < 1 or page_size < 1 already preserves empty/invalid inputs returning []. Pages beyond the last page naturally yield [] via slicing. Add a new regression test file covering the stated contracts.

edits.old:
start = page * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]
edits.new:
start = (page - 1) * page_size
    return items[start : start + page_size]

patches.rationale: The paginate function already uses one-based page numbering via start = (page - 1) * page_size, but it returns a slice of the input. When the input is a range object, slicing returns a range, not a list. The issue requires paginate(range(1,8), 2, 2) to return [3,4] (a list). The fix is to materialize the slice as a list. This preserves empty/invalid input behavior (returns []) and beyond-last-page behavior (empty list). Existing tests in tests/test_contract.py compare against [] and pass either way, but the new regression tests require list results. I will edit pagination.py to wrap the slice in list(). The existing regression test file already covers all acceptance contracts; I will add a new regression test file with additional coverage including exact type assertions and the literal input expression range(1,8).

review_results.summary: The diff changes paginate to one-based page numbering via start = (page - 1) * page_size and wraps the slice in list(...), so range inputs now return lists. The new regression test file covers the literal example paginate(range(1,8), 2, 2) == [3,4], one-based first page, empty input, invalid page/page_size, beyond-last-page, and last partial page. Regression evidence shows the same added tests failed on the original source (range(5,7) vs [3,4], etc.) and pass on the candidate, confirming the fix addresses the reported bug. Existing contract tests (empty input, page 0) remain satisfied.
concerns: The list(...) wrapping is a slight behavior change for non-list iterables (previously returned a range/slice object), but it is consistent with the issue's stated expected output type [3,4] and is covered by the added isinstance(result, list) assertions.
No existing public callers were found in the provided context, so caller compatibility could not be independently verified beyond the existing test_contract.py.
